name: strict-current-installed-v1
purpose: Current exact-wheel installed qualification using unchanged collectors and functional scenarios; no native production.
reuse: Reuse reviewed Windows6de6d77f/Linuxb728b575 wheels, existing CPython base interpreters, retained hash-locked dependency wheels, original handle-fidelity controls and patched Mesa9c5. Do not rebuild native code or SDKs, refresh dependency versions, clone sources or copy old environments/history.
consumer: One isolated consumer per registered platform run is necessary because prior disposable installs were cleaned and the strict launcher invokes an isolated installed Python. Create it only inside registered build/work/<run-id>, install the selected wheel and retained locked runtime closure offline in copy mode, then run both selected workflows in that same environment. Do not modify an existing pinned environment.
checks: Discovery, actual runtime/absence gates, exact installed inventory/dependency receipt, then replay with the bound receipt. Keep every attempt; at most two receipt extensions for genuinely newly loaded files, with all other gates passing. Require identical environment fingerprints across state/resource/failure and capture workflows. Never promote UNVERIFIED, failure, or another wheel/profile.
guards: Check shared scratch and declared additional allocation plus C:/D: capacity with registry613. WSL also checks guest filesystem and backing volume. Tolerate only disappearing test-owned files during size sampling. Stop owned child on capacity, timeout or I/O failure; record actual exit and wait.
cleanup: Retain exact producer/scenario/controller inputs, immutable dependency references, source/licenses, all failed reports and a reproducer. Preserve runtime/receipt/worker/native-trace originals outside scratch. Inspect and apply exact bounded cleanup plan, rehash retained files and report reclaimed bytes before the next experiment.
scope: Local strict observations only. Candidate source/scope/reuse approval is already bound; strict subject/profile joins, eight mandatory rows, required frozen-head CI, independent promotion, protected integration and delivery remain separate gates. Physical Linux GPU/Metal graphics and full parity remain unqualified.
